def-fd-positive-convolution-fluid-filter:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic torus convention used here. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and let $L>0$ be a period length. Put $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$, with normalized Haar measure $d\mu_L=L^{-d}\,dx$; writing $y=x/L$ and $\xi=2\pi y$ identifies this normalized measure with normalized Haar measure on $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, the periodic Fourier convention fixed in the referenced Fourier-Sobolev definition. Let $K:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, vanish outside a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)\,ds=1$. For $0<\ell<L/2$, define the periodized kernel

$$G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}\ell^{-d}K\!\left(\frac{r+Ln}{\ell}\right),\qquad r\in\mathbb T_L^d.$$

For a field $q$ with finitely many real components, each smooth and $L$-periodic, define its filtered field by

$$\overline q_\ell(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)q(x-r)\,dx=L^d\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)q(x-r)\,d\mu_L(r).$$

Here $dx$ is the volume measure on one period cell. For any smooth periodic vector field $u:\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^d$, define the subfilter stress and transfer by

$$\tau_\ell=\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell,\qquad \Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell,$$

where $(u\otimes v)_{ij}=u_i v_j$, $(\nabla v)_{ij}=\partial_jv_i$, and $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$. When $u$ is divergence-free and satisfies the incompressible evolution used in the resolved-energy balance, the sign convention makes positive $\Pi_\ell$ correspond to loss of resolved kinetic energy through the stress term. With length in metres and time in seconds, $x,L,\ell$ have units m, $u$ has units m s$^{-1}$, $G_\ell$ has units m$^{-d}$, $\tau_\ell$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, and $\Pi_\ell$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-3}$. The nonnegative-kernel hypothesis is part of this definition; no positivity or transfer-sign property is assigned to signed kernels or sharp spectral cutoffs.
lem-fd-periodic-filter-normalization-and:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice required by the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$, and $d\mu_L=L^{-d}dx$. Let $K:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, with $\int K(s)\,ds=1$, and let $0<\ell<L/2$. Define $G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}\ell^{-d}K((r+Ln)/\ell)$ and $\overline q_\ell(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)q(x-r)\,dx$. The locally finite sum defining $G_\ell$ is smooth, nonnegative, and $L$-periodic, and $\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)\,dx=1$. For every smooth periodic finite-dimensional field $q$, the filter also has the Euclidean representation

$$\overline q_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)q(x-\ell s,t)\,ds,$$

where $q$ on the right is its periodic lift. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is open and each component of $q:I\times\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^m$ and of its time derivative has continuous spatial derivatives of every order, then the filtered field has the same regularity and, for every spatial multi-index $\beta$,

$$\partial_x^\beta\overline q_\ell=\overline{\partial_x^\beta q}_\ell,\qquad \partial_t\partial_x^\beta\overline q_\ell=\overline{\partial_t\partial_x^\beta q}_\ell.$$

For every $\gamma>0$, the kernel moments

$$M_\gamma:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)|s|^\gamma\,ds,\qquad N_\gamma:=\max_{1\le j\le d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\partial_jK(s)|\,|s|^\gamma\,ds$$

are finite.
thm-fd-filtered-covariance-energy:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice required by the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$, and $d\mu_L=L^{-d}dx$. Fix $0<\ell<L/2$ and let $K:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, with $\int K(s)\,ds=1$. Define $G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}\ell^{-d}K((r+Ln)/\ell)$ for $r\in\mathbb T_L^d$ and, for every smooth periodic finite-dimensional field $q$, $\overline q_\ell(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)q(x-r)\,dx$. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval and let $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^d))$ be any smooth periodic vector field. Define

$$\tau_\ell=\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell,\qquad \Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell.$$

For $\delta_su(x,t):=u(x-\ell s,t)-u(x,t)$ and $m_\ell(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)\delta_su(x,t)\,ds$, the stress has the exact covariance form

$$\tau_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)\,\delta_su(x,t)\otimes\delta_su(x,t)\,ds-m_\ell(x,t)\otimes m_\ell(x,t).$$

It is symmetric and positive semidefinite at every $(x,t)$.

For the additional conclusions below, suppose $\nu>0$ is a constant kinematic viscosity, $p$ and $f$ are smooth scalar and vector fields on $I\times\mathbb T_L^d$, respectively, and $u$ satisfies pointwise

$$\partial_tu+\nabla\cdot(u\otimes u)+\nabla p=\nu\Delta u+f,\qquad \sum_i\partial_i u_i=0,$$

where $(\nabla\cdot T)_i:=\sum_j\partial_jT_{ij}$, $\nabla\cdot v:=\sum_i\partial_iv_i$, and $\Delta:=\sum_j\partial_j^2$. Here $p$ is pressure per unit mass and $f$ is force per unit mass. In SI dimensions, $x,L,\ell$ are in m, $t$ in s, $u$ in m s$^{-1}$, $p$ in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, $\nu$ in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, and $f$ in m s$^{-2}$. 

The filtered field satisfies

$$\partial_t\overline u_\ell+\nabla\cdot(\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell)+\nabla\overline p_\ell=\nu\Delta\overline u_\ell-\nabla\cdot\tau_\ell+\overline f_\ell,\qquad \nabla\cdot\overline u_\ell=0.$$

Writing $e_\ell=|\overline u_\ell|^2/2$, the pointwise resolved-energy balance is

$$\partial_t e_\ell+\sum_j\partial_j\!\left(e_\ell\overline u_{\ell,j}+\overline p_\ell\overline u_{\ell,j}-\nu\sum_i\overline u_{\ell,i}\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}+\sum_i\overline u_{\ell,i}\tau_{\ell,ij}\right)=-\nu|\nabla\overline u_\ell|_F^2+\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell+\overline f_\ell\cdot\overline u_\ell,$$

where $|A|_F^2:=\sum_{i,j}|A_{ij}|^2$. Consequently, for every $t\in I$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\frac12\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}|\overline u_\ell|^2\,d\mu_L+\nu\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}|\nabla\overline u_\ell|_F^2\,d\mu_L=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell\,d\mu_L+\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\overline f_\ell\cdot\overline u_\ell\,d\mu_L.$$

The forward-transfer sign convention is $\Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell$; this theorem makes no sign assertion for $\Pi_\ell$.
thm-fd-holder-energy-transfer-bound:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice required by the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, and $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized Haar measure $d\mu_L=L^{-d}dx$. Let $K:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, vanish outside a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int K(s)\,ds=1$. For $0<\ell<L/2$, use the periodized filter

$$G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}\ell^{-d}K\!\left(\frac{r+Ln}{\ell}\right),\qquad \overline q_\ell(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell(r)q(x-r)\,dx.$$

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and let $u:I\times\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^d$ have continuous time derivative and continuous spatial derivatives of every order. Define

$$\tau_\ell=\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell,\qquad \Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell.$$

For $0<\alpha<1$, let $A:I\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable and assume that for every $(x,t)\in\mathbb T_L^d\times I$ and every $s\in\operatorname{supp}K$,

$$|u(x-\ell s,t)-u(x,t)|\le A(t)\ell^\alpha|s|^\alpha.$$

Using the finite dimensionless kernel moments $M_\gamma=\int K(s)|s|^\gamma\,ds$ and $N_\gamma=\max_j\int|\partial_jK(s)|\,|s|^\gamma\,ds$, define $C_{d,K,\alpha}:=d^2(M_{2\alpha}+M_\alpha^2)N_\alpha$. Then for every $(x,t)$,

$$|\Pi_\ell(x,t)|\le C_{d,K,\alpha}A(t)^3\ell^{3\alpha-1}.$$

For every compact interval $J\subset I$ with $A^3\in L^1(J)$,

$$\int_J\|\Pi_\ell(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d)}\,dt\le C_{d,K,\alpha}\ell^{3\alpha-1}\int_J A(t)^3\,dt.$$

Consequently this upper bound tends to zero as $\ell\downarrow0$ when $\alpha>1/3$. At $\alpha=1/3$ it is scale-independent and gives no decay conclusion. With $x,L,\ell$ measured in m, $t$ in s, and $u$ in m s$^{-1}$, the Hölder factor $A$ has units m$^{1-\alpha}$ s$^{-1}$, the moments and constant $C_{d,K,\alpha}$ are dimensionless, and $\Pi_\ell$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-3}$. The estimate is conditional on the stated Hölder increment bound; it neither supplies that bound nor proves an endpoint conservation theorem, a turbulent $4/5$ law, or positive anomalous dissipation.
